newsitem.title: UK: NatWest to securitise 5$ bln corporate loans.
newsitem.headline: NatWest to securitise 5$ bln corporate loans.

text.p: NatWest Markets, the broking arm of National Westminster Bank, said on Wednesday it plans to securitise about five billion dollars of NatWest's corporate loans to release capital to the banking group.

The transaction means NatWest will transform corporate loans into stg and dollar-denominated floating rate notes and commercial paper, issued into the Eurobond market as well as the U.S. 144A private placement market.
"This transaction is a significant step in removing low margin assets from the balance sheet," Derek Wanless, NatWest's group chief executive, said in a statement.

The securitisation will free about 200 million stg of the group's capital, a NatWest Markets spokeswoman said without giving details. The Financial Times quoted Wanless as saying the money could be used to buy back shares or for acquisitions.

Martin Owen, chief executive at NatWest Markets, described the transaction as highly innovative, claiming it was the first time a bank had transformed "high quality investment grade" corporate loans into floating rate notes.
